subject: Hosted API quickstart: capacity, concurrency, and sandbox next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API quickstart: capacity, concurrency, and sandbox next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you into a hosted pilot quickly: 

1) Scope we covered: product search re-ranking + summarization for returns workflow (short prompts, ~250 tokens avg).
2) Immediate asks you had: a) confirmation of per-endpoint concurrency and burst behavior, b) guidance on token-based pricing for short/long responses, c) a sandbox endpoint with a reasonable rate cap to validate traffic patterns.

Proposed next actions:
- Redwood will provision a hosted sandbox endpoint scoped to a 3-day pilot with a 500 requests/min soft cap and a 2k reqs/min burst window.
- We’ll share an endpoints quickstart doc (attached) with suggested client-side concurrency patterns and best practices for prefix caching.
- Please confirm whether you want the sandbox traffic routed in us-west (default) or eu-west for latency testing.

If you confirm sandbox + region, Marissa will send the endpoint and credentials and Ben will attach a minimal evaluation matrix that maps your scenarios to expected token volumes.

Thanks — Jordan
--
Jordan Blake | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlasretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rivera <pri.rivera@atlasretail.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart: capacity, concurrency, and sandbox next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying things from our side: 

- Region: start with us-west so we can compare to our staging services in the same region.
- Rate caps: 500 reqs/min for normal test traffic is fine; the 2k burst sounds ok but can you confirm how long a burst is allowed (seconds/minutes) and whether requests that hit the burst are throttled vs queued?
- Concurrency: our frontend will run up to 40 concurrent inflight requests during peak simulated tests. Will a single hosted endpoint handle that or do you recommend multiple endpoints/routes?

Also, procurement asked for a playbook showing simple trial terms (duration, data handling, cancellation) we can attach to our vendor review. Can you include that?

— Sam
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart: capacity, concurrency, and sandbox next steps

Hi Sam — happy to take the endpoint provisioning and ops details. Answers below plus what we’ll deliver this week:

- Burst window: our hosted sandbox supports short bursts up to a 2k requests/min sustained for 1 minute before soft throttling begins. Soft throttling returns a 429 with Retry-After; we can enable a short queuing policy for the pilot if you prefer non-failing behavior (will increase tail latency).
- Concurrency guidance: a single hosted endpoint can handle 40 concurrent clients for your workload given our running kernel selection, but we recommend pinning concurrency per client to ~10 parallel HTTP connections and using a client-side retry/backoff to smooth spikes. If you expect sustained high concurrency across many clients, we can create two logical endpoints (same model) and split traffic.
- Procurement playbook: attaching a short trial terms stub and the quickstart endpoints doc. The trial is non-binding, 3 days by default, with standard data handling (retained for 30 days, not used for model training).

Deliverables this week:
- Hosted sandbox endpoint + temporary key (Marissa)
- Evaluation matrix template (Ben)
- Trial terms one-pager (attached)

If that looks good, confirm region and we’ll spin up the sandbox today.

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-quickstart-endpoints.pdf
Attachment: trial-terms-onepager.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlasretail.com>, Priya Rivera <pri.rivera@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart: capacity, concurrency, and sandbox next steps

Sam/Priya — attaching a lightweight evaluation matrix (atlas-eval-matrix.xlsx) that maps your three test scenarios to expected tokens/reqs and suggested concurrency buckets. A couple small asks for the sandbox run so we can instrument usage: 

- Can you share a representative sample of typical prompt lengths (avg tokens) for the re-ranking flow and the returns summarizer by end of day Monday? Helps with throughput knobs.
- Do you have a preferred Grafana or Datadog read-only endpoint we can push pilot metrics to, or should we share Redwood console access?

We’ll provision the sandbox in us-west once you confirm. Looking forward to seeing traffic.

— Ben
--
Ben Carter | Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachment: atlas-eval-matrix.xlsx
